Roughly $650m of Barbours Cut spend is planned for 2023-2027.
why_you_care: Per-foot berth capex benchmark for terminal work like LOGISTEC/Termont, and an early signal on where new Gulf container capacity is being added.

headline: Partners Group closes fourth direct infrastructure programme at more than $15bn
players: Partners Group held a final close on more than $15bn for its fourth direct infrastructure programme, focused on building next-generation energy, utility and other infrastructure platforms with an emphasis on mid-market opportunities. Investors included public and corporate pension plans, sovereign wealth funds, insurers, endowments, foundations, GPs, consultants and banks across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia Pacific. Deployment to date was not disclosed.
why_it_matters: Partners Group closed its fourth direct infrastructure programme above $15bn, targeting next-generation energy and utility platforms with a mid-market emphasis; deployment undisclosed. Close to half sits in separate accounts rather than the commingled fund, which is how headline programme sizes keep growing while pension commitment counts fall. That is $15bn of fresh bid pressure on already crowded digital and power auctions.
why_you_care: Another $15bn of bid pressure on already crowded digital and power auctions, with close to half sitting in separate accounts rather than the commingled fund.

headline: EQT secures $9.4bn for its AI-focused infrastructure fund
players: Infrastructure Investor reported on July 20, 2026 that EQT had secured $9.4 billion for an AI-focused infrastructure fund. The same briefing noted GIP had a record busy year and that IFM is targeting $2 billion for a value-add strategy. EQT had earlier been reported on June 8, 2026 to be targeting €21 billion for an upcoming fund.
why_it_matters: Dedicated AI infrastructure vehicles are now their own fundraising category rather than a sleeve inside flagship funds, and $9.4bn in three months says LPs will take concentrated thematic exposure at scale. That capital is the main driver of entry multiples in digital infrastructure and why co-located generation rights command a premium. The risk is vintage concentration into a finite set of powered sites.
why_you_care: EQT arming itself with $9.4bn aimed squarely at AI infrastructure, the capital that will bid entry multiples on powered land and generation rights against MSIP.

headline: Port of Oakland June loaded container volume up 10.3% on import and agricultural export growth
players: The Port of Oakland handled 181,356 TEU in June 2026, up 7.7% year on year, with loaded containers up 10.3% to 143,254 TEU. Full imports rose 11.1% to 78,114 TEU and full exports rose 9.3% to 65,140 TEU, while empties fell 1.1%. Vessel calls rose to 81 from 77. First-half 2026 volume was 1,114,665 TEU, down 2.5%, though loaded cargo grew 0.3%. Acting Maritime Director Jason Garben described June as a solid month with growth in both imports and exports.
why_it_matters: Oakland is the one major West Coast gateway where loaded exports, 65,140 TEU in June, are close to half of loaded volume, so it reads real demand better than Los Angeles or Long Beach. Exports up 9.3% says Californian agricultural cargo is moving despite freight rate and tariff noise, relevant to cold storage and agricultural transload in the Central Valley corridor. First-half volume still fell 2.5%, so the recovery is recent and thin.
why_you_care: Throughput read for terminals: loaded volume up 10.3% with exports near half the mix, though first-half volume still fell 2.5%, so the recovery is recent and thin.

headline: Epiroc Q2 orders up 13% with equipment orders up 30% organically and 20.1% adjusted operating margin
players: Epiroc reported second quarter 2026 orders received of SEK 17,305 million, up 13% and 13% organically, against SEK 15,276 million a year earlier, with large orders above SEK 150 million totalling SEK 720 million versus SEK 230 million. Revenues rose 10% to SEK 16,702 million, up 11% organically with a 1% currency headwind. Operating margin reached 19.9% from 18.7% and adjusted operating margin 20.1% from 19.7%. Equipment orders surged 30% organically, driven by copper and gold prices, with exploration strongest and service demand described as solid. The report was published July 17, 2026.
why_it_matters: Q2 orders of SEK 17,305m were up 13%, but equipment orders rose 30% organically, so growth is concentrated in capital goods rather than aftermarket, a late-cycle signature with more downside when metals turn. Adjusted operating margin was 20.1% against 19.7%. Exploration was strongest, and exploration leads mine development by years, supporting a multi-year runway for ground support, consumables and underground contracting.
why_you_care: Cycle read on your Jennmar/Weber lane: exploration strength supports a multi-year runway for ground support and consumables, but 30% organic equipment growth is a late-cycle signature.

headline: ECP VI reaches $7bn and LPs approve raising the hard cap to $7.8bn as the fund targets an $8bn close
players: Energy Capital Partners had raised $7 billion for ECP VI as of July 17, 2026, against an original $5 billion target, and LPs approved lifting the hard cap from $7.5 billion to $7.8 billion. The fund invests in energy infrastructure across North America and Europe, spanning energy transition, renewables, solar, wind, storage and natural gas. Dakota reported the fund at $4.8 billion in May 2026 approaching a summer final close.
why_it_matters: ECP had raised $7bn for ECP VI by July 17 against a $5bn original target, and LPs approved lifting the hard cap from $7.5bn to $7.8bn; Dakota had it at $4.8bn in May. The mandate spans renewables, storage and gas across North America and Europe, the flexibility LPs now want given dispatchable gas serving data centre load. The capital has a home: ECP co-bids with KKR on the GBP5.75bn DCC Energy take-private.
why_you_care: LP appetite in energy infrastructure read straight: a $5bn target heading toward $8bn, mandated across gas, renewables and storage, the flexibility data centre load now demands.

headline: Ratepayer advocates from five states attack FERC's show cause order for failing to remedy data center cost shifts
players: On July 17, 2026 state ratepayer advocates from Delaware, Illinois, Maryland, Ohio and Pennsylvania filed responses in Docket EL26-67 arguing FERC's June show cause order to PJM failed to address cost allocation for network upgrades driven by data centers. They argued it is 'arbitrary and capricious and contrary to the Federal Power Act' for the Commission to conclude it has a duty to address the risk of cost shifting among transmission customers while failing to remedy the actual cost shifts.
why_it_matters: Who pays for data-centre-driven network upgrades, load or the interconnecting customer, is worth billions across PJM alone, and advocates from five states argue FERC's June show cause order failed to fix it. If they prevail, large loads absorb far more of the cost and data centre total cost of ownership rises. If FERC leaves it, socialised costs persist and invite state legislative retaliation.
why_you_care: Docket EL26-67 decides whether large loads or other transmission customers fund data-centre network upgrades, which moves total cost of ownership in every data centre power model you build.

headline: Sandvik posts record Q2 with 17% organic order growth and adjusted EBITA margin of 22.6%
players: Sandvik reported second quarter 2026 order intake of SEK 37,799 million, up 17% organically, and revenues of SEK 36,752 million, up 23% organically at fixed exchange rates. Adjusted EBITA reached SEK 8,306 million against SEK 5,629 million a year earlier, lifting the adjusted EBITA margin to 22.6% from 19.0%. Adjusted diluted earnings per share were SEK 4.59. Free operating cash flow fell to SEK 3,590 million from SEK 5,090 million. The report was signed by CEO Stefan Widing on July 17, 2026.
why_it_matters: Sandvik's Q2 order intake was SEK 37,799m, up 17% organically, with revenue of SEK 36,752m, up 23% organically at fixed FX. Adjusted EBITA rose to SEK 8,306m from SEK 5,629m, lifting margin to 22.6% from 19.0%, and adjusted diluted EPS was SEK 4.59. Free operating cash flow fell to SEK 3,590m from SEK 5,090m, so working capital is absorbing the growth.
why_you_care: Cycle read for Jennmar/Weber Mining, the consumables thesis you underwrote: 17% organic order growth and margin up to 22.6%, but free cash flow fell as working capital absorbed growth.

headline: BofA: US needs 230+ GW of new capacity by 2030 against ~93 GW planned, leaving a 100-GW-plus shortfall
players: Bank of America analysis reported July 17, 2026 estimates the US needs more than 230 GW of new generating capacity through 2030 while utilities plan only about 93 GW, a shortfall exceeding 100 GW. Data centers alone are expected to add roughly 125 GW of electric demand, driving overall electricity demand growth of 4.1% compounded from 2026 to 2030. More than 7.5 GW of data center projects with on-site generation are already under construction, with another 60 GW-plus in pre-construction. Large gas turbines are described as largely sold out through 2030, pushing adoption toward reciprocating engines from Caterpillar, INNIO, Rolls-Royce and Wärtsilä; utilities are extending coal operations in Maryland, Wisconsin, Indiana, Utah, Kansas, Nebraska and Mississippi.
why_it_matters: BofA puts US capacity needs above 230 GW through 2030 against roughly 93 GW planned, a gap of more than 100 GW, with data centers alone adding about 125 GW of demand and total demand compounding 4.1%. That scarcity supports merchant spark spreads, capacity value and any firm capacity rights. Large gas turbines are largely sold out through 2030, pushing buyers toward reciprocating engines, and some utilities are extending coal.
why_you_care: The scarcity thesis in one number, 230-plus GW needed against roughly 93 GW planned, and the macro sitting under any gas-to-power or behind-the-meter underwriting.

headline: FERC directs NERC to develop reliability standards for large computational loads by end of 2026
players: At its July 16, 2026 open meeting FERC directed NERC to submit reliability standards addressing the most essential reliability challenges from computational large loads by December 31, 2026, and to revise its registry rules. At the same meeting FERC ordered CAISO and SPP to file a joint report on seams coordination with a 30-day public comment period, and approved streamlined NEPA procedures and expanded categorical exclusions for minor hydropower actions.
why_it_matters: Mandatory reliability standards for computational large loads, due from NERC by December 31, would make ride-through, voltage and frequency performance enforceable rather than contractual for the first time. That means real capex at data centres, covering power electronics, UPS and controls, and a compliance risk buyers have to diligence. The context is the July 23 Virginia line fault that dropped roughly 3GW of data centre load.
why_you_care: An unpriced retrofit liability forming inside operating data centre portfolios, as ride-through, voltage and frequency performance moves from contractual to enforceable by December 31.

headline: Avangrid promotes Ryan Shields to SVP Finance & Corporate Development and Teresa Bradford to SVP & Controller
players: Avangrid announced that Ryan Shields, previously SVP of Corporate Development, was promoted to Senior Vice President, Finance & Corporate Development, and Teresa Bradford, previously VP, Strategic Initiatives Controller, was promoted to Senior Vice President & Controller, both effective July 15, 2026 and reporting directly to the CEO. Shields will oversee treasury, corporate development, sustainability, financial strategy, capital allocation and long-term growth initiatives. The company described the change as a return to Avangrid's previous organizational model.
why_it_matters: Avangrid put treasury and corporate development under one SVP, Ryan Shields, reporting to the CEO, the structure a company adopts when capital allocation and transactions run as a single workstream; Teresa Bradford becomes SVP and Controller. The release cites continuity on key strategic projects and transactions but names no assets, and no renewables divestiture or ArcLight transaction was announced in the review period.
why_you_care: You covered ArcLight/Avangrid. Shields now runs treasury and corporate development as one workstream reporting to the CEO, so he is the counterparty on any Iberdrola North American portfolio rotation.

headline: Fitch cuts Brightline Florida senior Opco bonds to CC as reserves are substantially depleted after July 1 payments
players: Fitch downgraded Brightline Florida's $2.219bn senior Opco bonds to CC from CCC, citing a very high probability that both issuers will be unable to fully fund the next debt service payments due on or before January 1, 2027. Fitch noted reserve accounts for both bond sets were substantially depleted to meet the July 1 payments. Concurrently bondholders agreed to move the AAFOH interest payment from July 15 to July 24 and the commuter mandatory redemption from July 14 to July 23, the 13th amended commuter indenture and fourth AAFOH supplement.
why_it_matters: Fitch cut Brightline Florida's $2.219bn senior Opco bonds to CC from CCC, citing a very high probability that both issuers cannot fully fund debt service due on or before January 1, 2027. Reserve accounts were substantially depleted to make the July 1 payments, so the structure paid out of its last buffer rather than operations. Bondholders also moved AAFOH interest to July 24 and the commuter redemption to July 23.
why_you_care: You ran Brightline. CC is where the $2.219bn senior Opco credit now sits, reserves substantially depleted, and January 1, 2027 is the date any recovery analysis hangs on.

headline: Blackstone launches dedicated APAC infrastructure platform, hires KKR's Ami Momaya to lead India
players: Blackstone launched a dedicated Asia Pacific infrastructure platform and hired Ami Momaya as Managing Director and Head of Infrastructure for India, its first dedicated infrastructure hire in the region. Momaya joins from KKR India, having previously worked at the National Infrastructure Investment Fund and spent 17 years at Morgan Stanley Investment Management. Blackstone's infrastructure business runs about $84bn of AUM with a long-term buy-and-hold approach across energy, transportation, digital, and water and waste, and already owns APAC data centre platform AirTrunk.
why_it_matters: Blackstone launched a dedicated Asia Pacific infrastructure platform and hired Ami Momaya from KKR India as Head of Infrastructure for India, its first dedicated infrastructure hire in the region. He came from the National Infrastructure Investment Fund and spent 17 years at Morgan Stanley Investment Management. With about $84bn of infrastructure AUM and AirTrunk already owned, this formalises origination in the one region where Blackstone has been a follower.
why_you_care: Competitor tracking: Blackstone formalising India origination with an NIIF- and KKR-trained hire adds bid pressure in a market that has run clubby.

headline: DOE court filing concedes $7.6B of clean energy grant cancellations were based on recipients' state political identity
players: In a July 15, 2026 court filing, the Department of Energy stated that its cancellation of 223 clean energy project grants worth $7.6 billion, noticed in October 2025, was based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient's state and not on any programmatic, statutory, cost-reduction or performance-based factor. All 223 cancelled grants were in states that voted for Kamala Harris in 2024. A judge had previously reversed DOE's cancellation of $82.1 million in clean energy grants as of June 12, 2026.
why_it_matters: DOE told a court that cancelling 223 grants worth $7.6bn rested solely on the political identity of the recipient's state, with no programmatic, statutory, cost or performance rationale. That is close to a concession under the Administrative Procedure Act and raises the odds cancelled awards are reinstated. More broadly it prices political-reversal risk into federal grants, so expect lenders to haircut or exclude uncommitted awards from base-case coverage.
why_you_care: Reason to underwrite federal grants at zero until disbursed, and to expect lenders to haircut uncommitted awards; political-reversal risk is now priced into any grant-dependent capital stack.

headline: Lightpath signs 10-year second anchor tenant on eastern Pennsylvania AI-grade fibre build, lifting regional capacity ~30%
players: Lightpath secured a second infrastructure tenant, described as a leading multinational data centre developer and operator, on its 100% underground multi-conduit build in the Susquehanna region of eastern Pennsylvania under a 10-year anchor agreement. The tenant will use more than 60% of the combined eastern Pennsylvania system and adds another multi-gigawatt campus, increasing planned regional capacity by roughly 30%. Dollar terms undisclosed.
why_it_matters: Lightpath signed a second infrastructure tenant, described as a leading multinational data centre developer and operator, to a 10-year anchor on its all-underground multi-conduit build in eastern Pennsylvania's Susquehanna region. The tenant will use more than 60% of the combined system and adds another multi-gigawatt campus, lifting planned regional capacity about 30%. Dollar terms undisclosed. A second tenant on a committed trench is mostly margin.
why_you_care: Multi-conduit option value proving out inside MSIP's portfolio: a second 10-year anchor taking over 60% of the system lifts planned regional capacity roughly 30% on committed trench.

headline: Port of Los Angeles posts busiest June on record at 1,002,734 TEU, up 12% year over year
players: The Port of Los Angeles handled 1,002,734 TEU in June 2026, its busiest June in 118 years and only the third month ever above one million containers. Loaded imports rose 13% to 530,558 TEU, loaded exports were flat at 126,365 TEU and empties rose 17% to 345,811 TEU. First-half 2026 volume was 5,122,603 TEU, up 3%. Executive Director Gene Seroka said the results came without vessel backlogs or cargo delays as shippers advanced cargo ahead of trade policy changes.
why_it_matters: Record throughput of 1,002,734 TEU with no congestion says the gateway absorbed peak volume inside existing terminal, drayage and rail capacity, which weakens the near-term case for new San Pedro capacity. The mix is weaker: imports up 13% and empties up 17% while loaded exports were flat, so this is tariff-driven pull-forward. First-half growth of only 3% against a 12% June means later months are being borrowed from.
why_you_care: Volume comp for LOGISTEC/Termont, with a caution. Imports up 13% and empties up 17% against flat loaded exports is tariff pull-forward, so do not anchor terminal underwriting to first-half run rates.

headline: Port of Long Beach June volume up 10.6% to 779,331 TEU as retailers front-load ahead of August tariffs
players: The Port of Long Beach moved 779,331 TEU in June 2026, up 10.6% year on year and its third-busiest June. Loaded imports rose 11% to 387,025 TEU, loaded exports fell 1.3% to 86,446 TEU and empties rose 14.1% to 305,860 TEU. First-half volume reached 4.83 million TEU, up 1.7%. Retailers accelerated shipments ahead of tariff increases expected in August, with the National Retail Federation forecasting US container imports could hit a record 2.47 million TEU in July.
why_it_matters: A 10.6% June against 1.7% first-half growth says the West Coast is running on borrowed volume, with retailers pulling shipments forward ahead of tariff increases expected in August. Loaded exports fell 1.3% while empties rose 14.1%, so the imbalance is widening, raising carrier repositioning costs and cutting backhaul revenue for drayage and intermodal. A record July then an August drop is a whipsaw.
why_you_care: Borrowed volume rather than growth: 10.6% in June against 1.7% for the half, all tariff front-loading, and widening empties cut backhaul revenue for drayage and intermodal.

headline: FTAI Infrastructure sets Q2 2026 results for August 5 after close, with call August 6
players: FTAI Infrastructure Inc. said it plans to announce second quarter 2026 financial results after the close of Nasdaq on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, with a management conference call on Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time.
why_it_matters: FTAI Infrastructure will report Q2 after the close on August 5, with a call August 6. It is the first disclosure point after the Tidewater close and with the Long Ridge sale pending, so expect an update on Q3 closing timing and regulatory approval for the $1.52bn MARA transaction. The deleveraging bridge, $1.16bn of Long Ridge debt eliminated plus roughly $300m of corporate repayment, is the focus.
why_you_care: Diary item on a name you covered at Rothschild: August 5 after the close, the first disclosure since Tidewater closed and with the Long Ridge sale pending.

headline: US rail traffic growth slows to 1.5% in week ending July 11 as carloads turn negative
players: AAR data for the week ending July 11, 2026 showed US traffic of 503,525 carloads and intermodal units, up 1.5% year on year. Carloads fell 0.4% to 223,040 while intermodal rose 3.0% to 280,485. Eight of ten carload categories gained, with metallic ores up 1,627 to 21,857 and nonmetallic minerals up 1,263 to 32,823, but coal fell 4,713 carloads to 53,527 and grain fell 1,197. Year-to-date US traffic through 27 weeks reached 13.65 million units, up 3.4%, with North American traffic of 18.79 million units up 2.9% and Mexican intermodal up 55.4% for the week.
why_it_matters: Weekly traffic grew just 1.5% to 503,525 units with carloads down 0.4%, a sharp deceleration from 7.2% in mid-June and the first clear sign the import pull-forward is fading and second-half volumes weaken. Coal fell 4,713 carloads and has dropped in both June and July, so that decline looks structural. Mexican intermodal up 55.4% for the week is the standout.
why_you_care: Volume backdrop for rail and terminals: 1.5% growth with carloads down 0.4% and coal off 4,713 is a real deceleration, and Mexican intermodal up 55.4% is the nearshoring print.

headline: Brightline West has raised about $5.5bn of a $21bn budget; completion target slips to late 2029
players: Brightline West has raised approximately $5.5bn against a $21bn total project cost for the 218-mile Las Vegas to Rancho Cucamonga corridor, leaving a reported $15.5bn gap, with a $6bn federal loan still awaiting approval. Director of public affairs Antonio Castelan said the project is advancing with contract execution. Named contractors include Atlas Technical Consultants and Las Vegas Paving on Nevada track, McCarthy Building Companies and Grimshaw Architects on the Las Vegas station, and HNTB and Whiting-Turner on the 200,000 sq ft Sloan maintenance facility.
why_it_matters: A $15.5bn gap on a $21bn budget does not close with the pending $6bn federal loan, and the slip to late 2029 removes the pre-Olympics deadline that was driving federal urgency. Equity is the binding constraint: banks are reportedly ready to sign but conditioned on RRIF execution, while RRIF disbursement itself needs equity in place. Meanwhile contracts are being executed against uncommitted capital. The November bond maturity is the near-term event.
why_you_care: The other half of your Brightline story. Equity is the binding constraint on a $15.5bn gap the pending federal loan does not close, and November's bond maturity is the near-term event.

headline: PJM's 2028/29 capacity auction clears at the $325/MW-day cap for a second time, with a 6.8-GW reserve shortfall
players: PJM's capacity auction for the 2028-2029 delivery year cleared at the $325/MW-day price cap and cost $16.4 billion, leaving the system 6.8 GW below its 20% installed reserve margin target. The auction procured only about 525 MW of new resources, including 208 MW of uprates to existing generation, versus 774 MW in the prior auction for 2027-2028, which cleared at the same cap with a 6.5 GW shortfall. Aurora Energy Research's Julia Hoos warned the current design 'doesn't work to bring online new capacity or stimulate demand response.'
why_it_matters: Two auctions in a row clearing at the $325/MW-day cap, with the shortfall widening to 6.8 GW and only about 525 MW of new resources procured, means PJM capacity revenue is administratively bounded rather than market-cleared. For owners of existing dispatchable generation that is capped but effectively assured revenue. For developers, capacity payments alone will not finance new build; bilateral large-load contracts are the route.
why_you_care: The pricing point for PJM dispatchable generation: two auctions capped at $325/MW-day with the shortfall at 6.8 GW means capacity revenue is bounded but effectively assured for existing owners.

headline: Holtec files for a Nasdaq IPO on its SMR-300 plans as the 800-MW Palisades restart nears completion
players: Holtec International filed an S-1 with the SEC to list on Nasdaq, per a July 15, 2026 report. Its 300-MW SMR-300 pressurized-water reactor is expected to receive regulatory approval in 2029 with first deployment in the early 2030s; Holtec claims a single-unit plant would need only 15 acres and three years to build. Separately, Holtec is restoring the 800-MW Palisades plant in Michigan — the first US effort to return a permanently shuttered reactor to service — supported by a $1.52 billion DOE Loan Programs Office award plus $400 million of DOE support for SMR-300 construction. As of July 10, 2026, Holtec had completed all major renovations with roughly 5,000 maintenance tasks outstanding, described as equivalent to a routine 34-day outage; the power sales contract begins next year. Holtec plans two SMRs at the Palisades site.
why_it_matters: Holtec filed an S-1 to list on Nasdaq. Its 300-MW SMR-300 is expected to be approved in 2029 and deployed in the early 2030s, so it cannot serve this decade's load growth. The near-term story is the 800-MW Palisades restart, the first US attempt to revive a shuttered reactor, backed by a $1.52bn DOE loan plus $400m for SMR-300, with major renovations done and power sales starting next year.
why_you_care: Holtec's listing will price the market's discount rate on pre-revenue SMR pipelines; the near-term substance is the 800-MW Palisades restart, not a reactor that arrives in the 2030s.

headline: GIP to acquire majority control of US community solar developer Summit Ridge Energy
players: Global Infrastructure Partners, part of BlackRock, agreed to acquire a majority and controlling interest in Summit Ridge Energy through its mid-market strategy; terms undisclosed. Summit Ridge operates more than 275 solar and energy storage facilities serving over 60,000 businesses, homes and municipalities across Midwest, Mid-Atlantic and New England markets, with more than 3GW of solar and storage operating and in development. Founder Steve Raeder remains CEO; close is subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals.
why_it_matters: GIP agreed to acquire a majority controlling interest in community solar developer Summit Ridge Energy through its mid-market strategy; terms undisclosed, founder Steve Raeder stays as CEO, close subject to conditions and approvals. Summit Ridge has more than 275 facilities, over 60,000 customers and 3GW-plus operating and in development. Revenue comes from many small subscribers at state tariffs, which diversifies counterparty risk but adds churn and billing complexity.
why_you_care: GIP used its mid-market strategy rather than the flagship, worth noting on vehicle choice. Community solar off state tariffs diversifies counterparty risk but adds churn and billing complexity.

headline: Abu Dhabi's ePointZero completes $2.25bn all-cash purchase of Traverse Midstream at 11.3x EBITDA
players: ePointZero, a subsidiary of Abu Dhabi's 2PointZero Group, completed its $2.25 billion all-cash acquisition of Traverse Midstream Partners on July 14, 2026, buying a 35% stake in the Rover Pipeline and a 25% stake in the Ohio River System, both operated by Energy Transfer. The seller was The Energy & Minerals Group. The transaction implied roughly 11.3x EV/EBITDA against a historical midstream range of 10-12x, with the Alerian Midstream index trading near 10.8x forward as of late May 2026.
why_it_matters: ePointZero, part of Abu Dhabi's 2PointZero, completed a $2.25bn all-cash purchase of Traverse Midstream from The Energy & Minerals Group, acquiring 35% of the Rover Pipeline and 25% of the Ohio River System, both Energy Transfer-operated. It implies roughly 11.3x EV/EBITDA against a 10-12x historical range and the Alerian Midstream index near 10.8x forward, a strong mark for passive, non-operated stakes.
why_you_care: Marks a passive, non-operated midstream stake at roughly 11.3x EBITDA against a 10-12x historical range, the comp for minority pipeline interests and evidence Gulf capital is setting price.

headline: Bond Buyer: Brightline Florida distress raises contagion risk for Brightline West as $6bn RRIF loan stays pending
players: Bond Buyer reports Brightline West's $21bn capital plan comprises roughly $4bn bank debt, $4bn other debt, $4bn equity and $3bn grants, with $2.5bn of bonds swapped last year carrying a November maturity. The $6bn RRIF loan remains pending, with USDOT stating the Build America Bureau continues to work with the sponsor to obtain information required for the creditworthiness review. Both projects sit under Brightline Holdings LLC, backed by Fortress Investment Group; Assured Guaranty insures $1.13bn of the Florida senior bonds.
why_it_matters: The shared Fortress parent is the transmission mechanism: a Florida in-court process would put Brightline West's sponsor credibility in front of the same federal underwriters running the RRIF creditworthiness review. The nearest hard date is the November maturity on $2.5bn of swapped bonds, independent of the RRIF timetable. Octus notes a large funding hole remains even if the $6bn RRIF closes, making the $4bn equity the real gating item.
why_you_care: Extends your Brightline work to the West project: the shared Fortress parent is the transmission mechanism, and the November maturity on $2.5bn of swapped bonds is the nearest hard date.

headline: PJM 2028/2029 capacity auction clears at the $325/MW-day cap and falls 6,831 MW short of the reliability requirement
players: PJM's 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction, announced July 14, 2026, cleared at $325/MW-day UCAP — the administratively set price cap negotiated with state governors and FERC — a 2.5% decrease from the prior year. It procured 138,318 MW through the BRA plus 10,864 MW from Fixed Resource Requirement regions for 149,182 MW total, at a cost of roughly $16.4 billion, with a 14.7% reserve margin. Cleared capacity fell 6,831 MW short of PJM's reliability requirement, the first time the entire RTO failed to meet the one-event-in-10-years standard.
why_it_matters: Clearing at the $325/MW-day cap while still falling 6,831 MW short of the reliability requirement, the first RTO-wide miss of the one-event-in-10-years standard, means PJM's price signal is no longer clearing supply and demand. For owners that caps merchant upside and compresses the option value in thermal and storage underwritten on uncapped scarcity pricing, pushing value toward bilateral contracts and co-located self-supply.
why_you_care: Core market context for any PJM asset you model: clearing at the cap while still missing the reliability requirement caps merchant upside and pushes value toward bilateral contracts.

headline: Blackstone, Apollo and KKR to invest $5.34bn for 49% of Williams' behind-the-meter Power Innovation JV
players: Williams agreed a $5.34bn investment from Blackstone and partners Apollo and KKR for a 49% non-controlling equity interest in its Power Innovation joint venture, with Williams retaining 51% and operational control. The commitment comprises $4.4bn representing 49% of growth capex plus $0.9bn of additional consideration. The JV holds five behind-the-meter projects, Socrates, Apollo, Aquila, Socrates the Younger and Neo, part of Williams' 6GW-plus backlog; Williams holds buyout rights in years seven to fourteen at Blackstone's outstanding investment balance.
why_it_matters: Structured equity dressed as a JV: Williams keeps 51% and control, and its buyout right in years seven to fourteen at Blackstone's outstanding investment balance caps sponsor upside, which is why three big managers could share the $5.34bn without competing on multiple. Behind-the-meter generation contracted to data centre load is the strongest cash-flow profile in US power now: long tenor, investment-grade counterparties, no merchant risk.
why_you_care: The structure to know cold: minority structured equity into midstream-sponsored power, where Williams' year seven to fourteen buyout right caps sponsor upside, which is why three managers shared $5.34bn without bidding up multiple.

headline: Texas PUC advances a 12CP transmission cost allocation methodology to replace the long-standing 4CP regime
players: RTO Insider reported on July 12, 2026 that the Texas Public Utility Commission is moving forward through rulemaking with a 12 Coincident Peak transmission cost allocation methodology, expanding from the current four coincident peak mechanism to twelve monthly peaks.
why_it_matters: The Texas PUC is moving through rulemaking toward twelve coincident peaks instead of four for transmission cost allocation. 4CP has driven ERCOT's summer peak-shaving economics for years, so 12CP removes much of that arbitrage and directly impairs revenue for batteries, backup generation and curtailment programmes built to avoid it. Large flat loads like data centers benefit as costs spread more evenly.
why_you_care: Changes the ERCOT storage revenue stack. 12CP strips out much of the peak-shaving arbitrage batteries and backup generation were built to capture; flag it in any Texas underwriting.

headline: Carlyle sells power and AI infrastructure platform Copia Power to EQT Infrastructure VII after five-year hold
players: Carlyle agreed to sell Copia Power to EQT Infrastructure VII; the announcement did not disclose terms, though press coverage put the deal at about $2.6bn. Copia has taken 2.6GW of assets into operation or construction and holds a pipeline of over 30GW, comprising more than 25GW of solar and storage, 7GW of natural gas generation and 9GW of grid-connected data centres. Carlyle built the platform from inception in 2021, a five-year hold.
why_it_matters: Carlyle agreed to sell Copia Power to EQT Infrastructure VII; terms undisclosed, though press coverage put it near $2.6bn. Copia has 2.6GW operating or in construction and a 30GW+ pipeline: 25GW+ solar and storage, 7GW gas, 9GW grid-connected data centres. Value sits in interconnection positions, land and permitting rather than operating cash flow, and the gas and data centre capacity is what makes it AI-adjacent. Built from inception in 2021, a five-year hold.
why_you_care: EQT, a direct rival, paying a reported $2.6bn for a development platform priced on 30GW of pipeline rather than EBITDA; interconnection, land and permitting are the value.

headline: MSIP to acquire majority stake in French waste and urban services platform Nicollin Environnement
players: MSIP agreed to acquire a majority stake in Nicollin Environnement, a French environmental services platform founded in 1945, with the Nicollin family retaining a minority position. Terms undisclosed; close expected Q4 2026 pending employee consultation and regulatory approvals. The business runs waste collection and sorting, urban street cleaning and water-related services across roughly 360 public contracts and 8,000 private clients, with about 4,800 employees and a 2,900-vehicle fleet. Paul Hastings and Natixis Partners advised MSIP; Clifford Chance and Rothschild & Co advised the family.
why_it_matters: Municipal waste and street cleaning concessions underwrite like regulated infrastructure: multi-year public tenders, inflation indexation, high incumbent renewal rates. The stated value creation is modernising a 2,900-vehicle fleet with capex recoverable through renewals, plus buy-and-build in a fragmented French market. Taking control alongside a founding family that keeps a minority is the standard French succession structure and typically prices below a competitive auction.
why_you_care: One to know walking in: MSIP taking control of French municipal waste concessions alongside the founding family, with fleet modernisation and bolt-ons as the value story. Close expected Q4 2026.

headline: Argo Infrastructure acquires eight-site C&I solar portfolio from NuGen, taking platform to 270MW
players: Argo Infrastructure Partners LP acquired an eight-site solar portfolio from NuGen Capital Management, LLC, comprising six sites in Massachusetts and two in New Jersey. Terms undisclosed. The acquisition expands Argo's commercial and industrial solar platform to 270MW across 196 sites. NuGen continues as a partner supporting asset performance post-close. Argo described the deal as its 21st investment since 2013.
why_it_matters: Argo Infrastructure bought an eight-site C&I solar portfolio from NuGen Capital Management, six sites in Massachusetts and two in New Jersey, terms undisclosed, taking its platform to 270MW across 196 sites and marking its 21st investment since 2013. NuGen stays on as operating partner post-close. Massachusetts SMART and New Jersey SREC-II supply 10-20 year contracted revenue largely insulated from merchant power prices.
why_you_care: Competitive-set read: a financial owner aggregating C&I solar to 270MW and keeping NuGen on as operator, buying SMART and SREC-II contracted revenue rather than building an asset management team.

headline: Hydrostor says Willow Rock is nearing groundbreaking later this year with a signed project labor agreement and Hatch as EPC-M
players: Hydrostor said the 500 MW, eight-hour Willow Rock Energy Storage Center in Kern County, California is nearing groundbreaking and construction later this year, with a project labor agreement already signed and Hatch acting as EPC-M partner while Hydrostor contracts directly with vendors and suppliers. The company hosted contractor and supplier open houses in Rosamond and Bakersfield, reporting interest from more than 40 local vendors. It cited over $500m of direct and indirect benefits to Kern County and approximately $18m in annual property taxes, with around 40 permanent operating positions.
why_it_matters: A signed project labor agreement and supplier outreach drawing more than 40 local vendors are pre-mobilisation activities, so this is a real construction-start signal. Under the EPC-M structure Hatch manages but Hydrostor contracts vendors directly, leaving procurement risk with the sponsor and making the financing package the gating item. Willow Rock anchors the DOE conditional commitment of up to $1.76bn and the 50 MW California Community Power offtake, so a slip reprices the platform.
why_you_care: Sharpest point on your Hydrostor thesis: a signed labour agreement and 40-plus vendors read as real pre-mobilisation, but EPC-M leaves procurement risk with the sponsor and financing gates it.

headline: Robotti & Company urges McDermott board to add oversubscription rights to $1.50 per share, 92% dilutive rights offering
players: Robotti & Company Advisors, holder of roughly 2% of McDermott's Class A ordinary shares, published a July 7 letter calling on the board to amend the rights offering to include an oversubscription privilege allocated pro rata ahead of the backstop parties. The offering contemplates up to 333.3 million new shares against 28.6 million outstanding at $1.50 per share, implying about $51m of pre-money equity value and roughly 92% dilution, backstopped by MFN Partners, Baupost Group, Mason Capital Management and First Pacific Advisors, two of which have board representation. Robotti argues the price massively undervalues a business with about $10bn of revenue, $489m of EBITDA, $17.6bn of backlog and a net cash balance sheet.
why_it_matters: Robotti, holding about 2% of McDermott's Class A shares, wants the rights offering amended to add an oversubscription privilege ranking ahead of the backstop parties. Without one, non-participating stock flows to insiders including MFN, Baupost, Mason and First Pacific, two with board seats, at $1.50, implying roughly $51m pre-money equity and about 92% dilution against $489m of EBITDA and $17.6bn of backlog. Subscription expires August 17, 2026.
why_you_care: Your McDermott/NMDC situation turned into a live minority-holder fight over a 92% dilutive rights offering at $1.50, with the subscription expiring August 17, 2026.

headline: Lightpath to build AI-grade fibre to two new hyperscale campuses in Michigan and Wisconsin, each above 1GW
players: Lightpath will deliver triverse fibre infrastructure and multi-terabit capacity to two new hyperscale data centre campuses in Saline, Michigan and Port Washington, Wisconsin, each expected to exceed 1GW of capacity. The Saline build targets completion by end-2026 and Port Washington in Q2 2027, under a partnership with an anchor hyperscale customer. Contract term and dollar value not disclosed.
why_it_matters: Lightpath will deliver triverse fibre and multi-terabit capacity to hyperscale campuses in Saline, Michigan by end-2026 and Port Washington, Wisconsin in Q2 2027, each above 1GW, under an anchor customer partnership; term and value undisclosed. Moving out of its legacy northeast metros changes the geographic risk and addressable market. Physical route diversity cannot be replicated quickly, which supports long terms and pricing power, but anchor-led greenfield eats equity ahead of cash flow.
why_you_care: Your platform moving out of its legacy northeast metros. Anchor-led greenfield eats equity ahead of cash flow, the thing to watch as Lightpath funds two campuses above 1GW.

headline: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to take 15% of Morrison with $500m fund investment and $1.5bn raising pact
players: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank agreed to acquire a 15% stake in infrastructure manager Morrison, alongside an initial $500m investment split across Morrison Value Add II and The Morrison & Co Infrastructure Partnership. The arrangement includes a $1.5bn capital-raising agreement between the two firms. Valuation of the 15% stake was not disclosed.
why_it_matters: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank agreed to take 15% of infrastructure manager Morrison, with an initial $500m split across Morrison Value Add II and The Morrison & Co Infrastructure Partnership, plus a $1.5bn capital-raising agreement. Stake valuation undisclosed. It is the familiar GP-stake-plus-distribution trade: SMTB buys management company economics and access, Morrison gets anchor capital and a Japanese channel that effectively de-risks its next two vintages.
why_you_care: GP-stake-plus-distribution: SMTB buys management company economics, Morrison gets anchor capital and a Japanese channel. Manager-level colour, with no read-through to what MSIP underwrites.

headline: Avangrid begins panel installation at 57 MWdc Oregon Trail Solar in Gilliam County, Oregon
players: Avangrid began installing over 100,000 panels at Oregon Trail Solar, a 57 MWdc / 41 MWac project in Gilliam County, Oregon, supporting 200 local union jobs during construction with completion expected in 2027. The project is expected to contribute $6m in combined payments in lieu of taxes and property taxes to Gilliam County over its life. Avangrid said it operates more than 2.5 GW of capacity in Oregon and has announced the adjacent Shutler Energy Storage project alongside the operating Pachwáywit Fields solar project. No offtaker or PPA counterparty was disclosed.
why_it_matters: Still building rather than harvesting: continued construction spend on the 57 MWdc / 41 MWac Oregon Trail Solar cuts against the thesis that Iberdrola is a net seller of North American assets. No offtaker was disclosed, which makes contracted cash flow quality hard to assess for any portfolio sale. Clustering Oregon Trail with the adjacent Shutler storage project and the operating Pachwaywit Fields solar creates a package that would sell better as a bundle.
why_you_care: Your ArcLight/Avangrid mandate: continued construction spend cuts against the net-seller thesis, no offtaker disclosed, and the Oregon cluster would sell better bundled than piecemeal.

headline: Fervo says drilling rates are up 143% since its first Cape Station well, targeting $3,000/kW long term
players: Fervo said on July 8, 2026 that its third-generation well design has increased drilling rates 143% versus its first Cape Station well, with the Sawtooth 7 well drilled in 21 days to 19,448 feet measured depth including a 7,500-foot lateral. The company projects Cape Phase II will deliver power at approximately $5,500 per kilowatt of installed capacity, with a longer-term target of $3,000 per kilowatt.
why_it_matters: Published capex-per-kW targets give investors a cost curve to underwrite instead of a technology story: roughly $5,500/kW at Cape Phase II heading toward $3,000/kW long term, where EGS competes with new-build combined cycle while delivering 24/7 output. Well-cost learning is the biggest driver of geothermal IRR, and the third-generation design drilled Sawtooth 7 in 21 days, lifting drilling rates 143% versus the first Cape Station well.
why_you_care: Sets the clean-firm cost curve at roughly $5,500/kW for Cape Phase II against a $3,000/kW long-term target, where EGS starts competing with new-build combined cycle.

headline: Meridiam and Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Trust launch energy decarbonisation partnership with no upfront NHS capital
players: Meridiam and Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust launched a strategic partnership to design, finance and deliver energy system upgrades, with Dalkia Energy Services as technical partner. Investment size and contract length were not disclosed. Scope covers replacing fossil-fuel heating with low-carbon alternatives, building energy efficiency improvements and energy network modernisation, initially at St Thomas' Hospital in South London with potential expansion to other NHS Trusts and public bodies in southeast London. The partnership requires no upfront investment from the NHS.
why_it_matters: Meridiam and Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust launched a partnership to design, finance and deliver energy upgrades, with Dalkia Energy Services as technical partner, starting at St Thomas' Hospital and potentially extending to other southeast London trusts and public bodies. Scope covers replacing fossil-fuel heating, efficiency works and network modernisation. No NHS capital upfront; size and contract length undisclosed.
why_you_care: Availability-style cash flow from a public counterparty with no NHS capital upfront and terms undisclosed, a read on the low-risk end of the curve, background rather than actionable.
companies: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust

headline: Quinbrook closes second UK renewables fund at £587m with 74% re-up rate
players: Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners held a final close of £587m for the Quinbrook Renewables Impact Fund, its second UK-focused renewables vehicle. Fundraising took roughly 18 months and the fund achieved a 74% re-up rate from investors in the predecessor strategy. Individual LP names were not disclosed.
why_it_matters: The 74% re-up rate is the real datapoint, showing UK value-add renewables held its LP base while generalist energy transition fundraising stalled. The £587m final close, raised in roughly 18 months, sizes the fund for build-and-operate solar, onshore wind and storage rather than trophy assets. Capacity market and CfD floors support leverage; grid connection dates are the execution risk.
why_you_care: Background only. The 74% re-up rate shows UK value-add renewables held its LP base, but nothing here is actionable unless a UK mandate crosses the desk.

headline: USDOT awards $1.73bn in BUILD grants across 127 projects with $136.8m to ports and $87.7m to rail
players: USDOT announced $1.73 billion in BUILD grants on July 8, 2026 across 127 infrastructure projects in 52 states, territories and the District of Columbia. Road and bridge projects took $1.3 billion or 77% of the total, with $169.9 million to transit, $136.8 million to port infrastructure, $87.7 million to rail and $11 million to aviation. Named awards included $24.3 million to the Port of Corpus Christi Authority to modernise and lengthen track at its inland port facility and $8.5 million to Alaska Railroad Corp. to widen the Port of Seward freight dock by 300 feet. USDOT received nearly 1,200 eligible applications requesting over $14.5 billion.
why_it_matters: Roads and bridges took 77% of the $1.73bn against 8% for ports and 5% for rail, a clear statement of federal priorities and a reason not to assume grants will materially de-risk freight or terminal capex. With nearly 1,200 applications chasing over $14.5bn, grant assumptions in project financings deserve a heavy discount and sponsors carry more of the capital stack themselves.
why_you_care: Discount grant assumptions heavily in freight and terminal underwriting. Roads and bridges took 77% against 8% for ports and 5% for rail, with nearly 1,200 applications chasing over $14.5bn.

headline: Pembina confirms Greenlight will supply dedicated gas-to-power for Meta's new Alberta data centre
players: Pembina Pipeline welcomed Meta's announcement of a new Alberta data centre project with the Government of Alberta, confirming that the Greenlight Electricity Centre partnership between Pembina, MSIP and Kineticor Asset Management will provide dedicated behind-the-meter gas-fired generation to the development. Pembina CEO Scott Burrows described dedicated, contracted gas-to-power infrastructure as a promising new growth platform. No incremental financial terms were disclosed.
why_it_matters: Pembina confirmed that Greenlight Electricity Centre, its partnership with MSIP and Kineticor, will supply dedicated behind-the-meter gas-fired generation to Meta's new Alberta data centre. Naming the hyperscaler de-risks the credit story, because counterparty quality decides whether this prices as contracted infrastructure or merchant Alberta power. Behind-the-meter also sidesteps AESO interconnection queues and transmission limits. No incremental financial terms were disclosed.
why_you_care: This is the MSIP position to know cold: Greenlight with Pembina and Kineticor supplying behind-the-meter generation to a named hyperscaler, which decides whether it prices as contracted infrastructure or merchant Alberta power.

headline: IFM completes Atlas Arteria takeover, reaching 67.43% voting power in the toll road group
players: IFM Global Infrastructure Fund's bid vehicle Diamond Infraco 1 closed its off-market offer for Atlas Arteria on 7 July 2026 with 67.43% voting power, including acceptances settling up to 21 days later. The offer began with a bidder's statement on 27 April 2026, was initially rejected by the Atlas Arteria board on 6 May, and was raised in June before the board recommended it. Atlas Arteria owns 30.8% of the 2,424km APRR/AREA/A79/ADELAC French motorway network, 66.67% of the Chicago Skyway, a 100% economic interest in the Dulles Greenway and 100% of Germany's Warnow Tunnel.
why_it_matters: IFM's bid vehicle closed its off-market offer for Atlas Arteria at 67.43% voting power, enough to drive distribution policy and refinancing without compulsory acquisition. The board rejected the offer on 6 May before IFM raised it in June and recommended it. The prize is the 30.8% APRR stake, inflation-linked French motorway tolls. Dulles Greenway, with capped tolls and traffic below underwriting, is the problem asset.
why_you_care: How core buyers price concession cash flow: 67.43% is enough to drive distribution policy and refinancing without compulsory acquisition, with inflation-linked APRR the prize and Dulles Greenway the problem asset.

headline: UP and NS file first round of STB supplemental responses, offering to relinquish control of jointly owned terminal railroads
players: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern filed the first tranche of responses to the STB's May 28 information request on July 7, 2026, addressing jointly owned entities including the Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis, Kansas City Terminal Railway and TTX Company. The carriers stated they will not control those entities post-merger and offered divestiture as an option. The filing reiterates a claim of $3.5 billion in annual shipper savings from single-line transcontinental service, with remaining responses due July 27 and completion targeted for mid-2027.
why_it_matters: UP and NS offering to give up control of TRRA, Kansas City Terminal and TTX is a real concession and a template for what the STB will extract on gateways and interchange. Terminal railroads and railcar-lessor assets inside those JVs could become divestiture candidates, a direct sourcing angle for infra funds. The $3.5bn shipper-savings figure is the applicants' own number and will be attacked, so do not underwrite it.
why_you_care: Forced-seller pipeline in rail: terminal railroads and railcar-lessor assets inside those JVs could come up for divestiture, a direct sourcing angle for MSIP. Discount the $3.5bn savings claim.

headline: Blackstone Energy Transition Partners to acquire Dresser Utility Solutions from First Reserve
players: Blackstone Energy Transition Partners agreed to acquire Dresser Utility Solutions from First Reserve; terms undisclosed. Founded in 1880 and headquartered in Houston, Dresser supplies metering and digital instrumentation, pressure and flow control, gas and water infrastructure repair products and utility software, employing roughly 850 people globally. Blackstone described it as the first investment from the latest vintage of its Energy Transition Partners private equity vehicle.
why_it_matters: Blackstone Energy Transition Partners agreed to acquire Dresser Utility Solutions from First Reserve; terms undisclosed. Dresser, Houston-based, founded 1880, roughly 850 staff, supplies metering and digital instrumentation, pressure and flow control, gas and water repair products and utility software. Revenue tracks utility maintenance and replacement capex, which is regulated rate-base spending and non-discretionary. As the first deal of a new fund vintage it points energy transition capital at picks-and-shovels rather than generation.
why_you_care: A rival opening a new fund vintage on picks-and-shovels rather than generation, with revenue tied to non-discretionary utility replacement capex. Where energy transition capital is actually going.

headline: InfraVia to acquire D-Marin, EMEA premium marina platform, from CVC Capital Partners VII
players: InfraVia Capital Partners agreed to acquire D-Marin from CVC Capital Partners VII. Terms undisclosed. D-Marin operates 28 premium marinas across nine countries including Turkey, Croatia, Greece, UAE, Spain, Italy, France, Malta and Albania, with over 14,300 berths of which more than 1,000 are dedicated superyacht berths, plus 12 professional boatyards servicing over 2,500 yachts annually. CVC acquired the business in 2020 and built it into the regional market leader.
why_it_matters: Marinas behave more like ports than leisure assets: concession or long-leasehold tenure, multi-year berth contracts, high renewal rates and effectively fixed supply because coastal permitting is near-impossible. InfraVia's levers are further consolidation of a fragmented market and yield management on the 1,000-plus superyacht berths where scarcity bites hardest. But CVC already ran the roll-up to 28 marinas in nine countries, so InfraVia is paying for a built platform. Terms undisclosed.
why_you_care: Sponsor-to-sponsor exit showing where infra money finds pricing power outside core sectors, though CVC already built the 28-marina platform, so InfraVia is paying for the roll-up rather than doing it.

headline: NERC's 2026 Summer Reliability Assessment flags New England and the Northwest at elevated risk in extreme scenarios
players: NERC's 2026 Summer Reliability Assessment projected all areas would have adequate resources under normal summer conditions but identified two US regions — New England and the Northwest — at elevated risk under extreme load scenarios. In a July 6, 2026 review, Grid Strategies argued the flagged regions would in fact hold between 5% and 93% more reserves than their target reserve margins once additional resources and mitigation measures were counted.
why_it_matters: Reliability assessments feed state procurement mandates, capacity market parameters and out-of-market emergency payments, so the label matters commercially even where the physics is contested. Elevated-risk flags on New England and the Northwest support the case for new peaking capacity, storage and demand response there. Grid Strategies counters that those regions hold 5% to 93% more reserves than target once mitigation is counted.
why_you_care: Points to peaker and storage demand in New England and the Northwest, with Grid Strategies' rebuttal a caution against underwriting scarcity revenue off a headline reliability flag.

headline: MSIP takes 47.5% of Greenlight Electricity Centre, a 932MW Alberta gas plant tolled to a data centre customer
players: MSIP announced an investment in the Greenlight Electricity Centre in Sturgeon County, Alberta, taking a 47.5% interest alongside Pembina Pipeline (47.5%) and Kineticor Asset Management (5%). Pembina's 2 July FID disclosure put gross project cost at approximately $4bn (about $4.6bn including financing costs), funded roughly 60% debt and 40% equity, with about $310m of annual run-rate adjusted EBITDA net to Pembina and around 85% of costs secured under fixed-price agreements. The 932MW combined-cycle plant will consume roughly 150 MMcf/d of gas, run on Siemens Energy turbines, sell under a long-term tolling agreement to a data centre customer and enter service in H2 2030; Pembina is construction and operations manager. Santander advised MSIP on M&A and financing, with Kirkland & Ellis and Bennett Jones as legal counsel.
why_it_matters: MSIP's largest disclosed 2026 commitment is development-stage rather than operating: a 932MW Alberta plant with four years of construction, so the return pays for completion risk, with fixed-price agreements covering about 85% of the roughly $4bn cost. A long-term toll to a data centre customer turns merchant Alberta power into contracted, availability-based cash flow, and 60/40 debt-equity implies about $1.8bn of equity across MSIP, Pembina and Kineticor.
why_you_care: MSIP's largest disclosed 2026 commitment, and the one most likely to land on your desk: four years of construction risk on a 932MW Alberta plant tolled to a data centre.

headline: PJM stakeholders advance registry-based backstop procurement but fail to agree on data center connect-and-manage
players: PJM stakeholders on July 2, 2026 approved a two-part reliability backstop procurement plan built on a registry-based subscription model developed by the Data Center Coalition and ten utilities including Dominion Energy, Duke Energy and Exelon. Utilities and load-serving entities can request PJM procure specific capacity through a one-time auction, with large loads billed for the cost and the procurement capped at $555/MW-day, preceded by a bilateral contracting phase. Stakeholders failed to reach consensus on a connect-and-manage framework for data centers, instead backing a large load registry giving state regulators data to set load-reduction priorities. PJM planned a board filing in July, a backstop auction in September 2026, and the 2029/30 capacity auction on December 9, 2026.
why_it_matters: PJM stakeholders approved a two-part reliability backstop built on a registry-based subscription model from the Data Center Coalition and ten utilities including Dominion, Duke and Exelon. Utilities and LSEs can ask PJM to procure capacity in a one-time auction capped at $555/MW-day, with large loads billed for it after a bilateral phase. No consensus on connect-and-manage. Board filing in July, backstop auction September, 2029/30 auction December 9.
why_you_care: Large loads become a named, creditworthy payer capped at $555/MW-day, which is the bankability argument for new gas-fired build in PJM and feeds straight into gas-to-power underwriting.

headline: FERC denies ArcLight-backed developer's waiver to modify a $2B PJM fast-track gas plant, enforcing RRI rigidity
players: FERC on July 2, 2026 denied a waiver sought by Advanced Power Services, owned by ArcLight Capital Partners, to reduce the maximum output of its roughly $2 billion Chestnut Run gas plant in Carroll County, Ohio from 1.3 GW to 1.245 GW after equipment supply constraints forced a turbine substitution. The project entered PJM's Reliability Resource Initiative, an expedited process that initially covered 51 projects totalling roughly 9.3-11.8 GW and prohibits changes to project size and capacity rights. FERC found studies from the equipment change would introduce substantial delays to Transition Cycle #2 with ripple effects across PJM's study schedule.
why_it_matters: FERC denied a waiver sought by ArcLight-owned Advanced Power Services to cut its roughly $2bn Chestnut Run gas plant in Ohio from 1.3 GW to 1.245 GW after supply constraints forced a turbine substitution. PJM's Reliability Resource Initiative bars changes to project size, and FERC found the restudy would delay Transition Cycle #2. Fast-track interconnection now clearly carries zero flexibility, raising the value of secured turbine slots.
why_you_care: Your ArcLight coverage. An RRI queue position is only as good as the turbine order locked behind it, and secured equipment slots just became more valuable.

headline: Aecon-led consortium wins EPC for MSIP-backed Greenlight plant, with Aecon's share at C$1.7bn
players: Tecnicas Reunidas Alberta (TRA), a consortium in which Aecon is majority partner, was awarded the EPC contract for the Greenlight Electricity Centre, with Aecon's share valued at $1.7bn. Scope covers civil, piping, mechanical, structural, electrical and instrumentation works plus the gas metering station, switchyard and substation. The project is owned by Greenlight Electricity Centre Limited Partnership (Pembina 47.5%, MSIP 47.5%, Kineticor 5%), is 932MW in its initial phase and is permitted for expansion to 1,864MW; construction starts Q3 2026 with completion anticipated in 2030.
why_it_matters: The EPC award converts FID into a real construction schedule and lets the equity be underwritten as infrastructure rather than development risk. Key detail: the site is permitted to 1,864MW against a 932MW first phase, making phase two a free option on brownfield expansion at an already-interconnected site. With contractor capacity the binding constraint on North American gas, locking an EPC now for 2030 is an edge.
why_you_care: MSIP owns 47.5% of this one. The EPC award moves Greenlight from development to construction risk, and the permit to 1,864MW against a 932MW phase one is free brownfield optionality.

headline: Brightline Florida taps reserves to make July 1 payments on senior munis and corporate notes, buys two weeks on commuter bonds
players: Brightline drew on reserves to make scheduled July 1 payments on its $2.2bn senior municipal bonds and $1.1bn corporate notes. It negotiated a two-week extension on the $985m commuter bonds, moving the mandatory tender deadline from June 30 to July 14 and the grace period to July 15. A further payment on the $1.2bn AAF Operations Holdings subordinate municipal bonds was due July 15, with an option to trigger a third deferred interest election.
why_it_matters: Brightline paid July 1 obligations on the $2.2bn senior munis and $1.1bn corporate notes out of reserves rather than cash flow, the point the capital structure stopped self-funding. It negotiated a two-week extension on the $985m commuter bonds, moving mandatory tender to July 14, which tells you where the company thinks the fulcrum sits. A third deferred-interest election on the $1.2bn AAFOH bonds is a contractual toggle needing no creditor consent.
why_you_care: Your Brightline deal at the inflection: July 1 paid out of reserves, not cash flow, and the two-week extension on the $985m commuter bonds shows where the fulcrum sits.

headline: McDermott prices $550m of 10.5% Nordic bonds due 2031 alongside a $500m fully backstopped rights offering
players: McDermott priced $550m of senior bonds at a 10.5% coupon maturing July 2031, with application to be made for listing on Euronext Nordic ABM. Net proceeds will be applied toward cash collateralising letter of credit facilities, refinancing existing debt and general corporate purposes. The bond forms part of a broader refinancing alongside a $500m equity rights offering fully backstopped by major shareholders, with an ex-rights date of July 10, record date and special shareholder meeting on July 13, and a subscription period expiring August 17, 2026 at 4:59 p.m. ET. Expected closing is the third quarter of 2026; DNB Carnegie acted as global coordinator and joint bookrunner with Clarksons Securities as joint bookrunner.
why_it_matters: A 10.5% coupon on senior paper, against $489m of trailing EBITDA and a net cash balance sheet, says the market still prices McDermott off its restructuring history. Use of proceeds is the tell: cash collateralising LC facilities is a bonding fix for a contractor that cannot get uncollateralised capacity. Over $1bn raised in total, including $500m of dilutive equity, with subscription expiring August 17 and Q3 closing expected.
why_you_care: Your McDermott situation, repriced. The 10.5% print is where that credit clears now, and cash-collateralising LC facilities says the bonding constraint still binds.
